title: Turning the control module off may not stop a character moving; also catch the movement keys
observation: For a spectator mode the client called PlayerModule:GetControls():Disable(), yet a held W (sent through Studio MCP's simulated keys) still walked the character 34 studs. Adding a ContextActionService binding above default priority that sinks W, A, S, D, Up, Down, Space, Thumbstick1 and ButtonA while spectating stopped it (0 studs), and unbinding it restored walking.
recommendation: When a mode must freeze the player's own character (spectating, cutscenes, menus), sink the movement inputs with a high-priority ContextActionService binding as well as disabling the controls, and verify by holding a movement key and measuring the character's position.
applies_when: A spectator, cutscene or menu mode must keep the player's character still
The game uses the default PlayerModule controls
limits: Seen only with Studio MCP's simulated keyboard input, which may reach the character differently from a real keyboard
Gamepad thumbsticks and touch were not tested

evidence.detail: Section 7: 34 studs moved with controls disabled, 0 with the movement keys also sunk, 28 after leaving.
